cohort: The study participants were 562 pregnant women, 203 of whom were infected with HBV, who attended the Affiliated Hospital of Guizhou Medical University in China between June 2020 and June 2023.
finding: Maternal HBV RNA level was identified as an independent risk factor for intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) in HBsAg-positive pregnant women, and HBsAg positive women had a higher risk of ICP compared to HBsAg negative women.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in the rates of mode of delivery between HBsAg positive and HBsAg negative pregnant women.
